content: Hide vs disable UI mistake: hide a feature only when the user has zero legitimate reason to know it exists; if the user CAN gain access later or sees the action performed by others in shared views, keep it visible but disabled with an explanation - hiding entirely causes layout shifts and confusion. Critical security mistake: treating client-side hide/disable as an authorization boundary - a determined user can still call the API directly bypassing any frontend-only check; RBAC must be enforced server-side, frontend role logic is purely UX polish and must be DERIVED from the same role data the backend returns (JWT/me payload), never duplicated independently.
